gloss: worship hall; oratory; hall of worship

definitions.gloss: worship hall; hall of worship; oratory
definitions.explanation: The main hall of a Shinto shrine where visitors pray and make offerings. It stands in front of the main sanctuary and is the building that most visitors interact with — the place where you throw coins, clap your hands, and bow in prayer.

examples.japanese: {拝殿|はいでん}の{前|まえ}で{手|て}を{合|あ}わせる。
examples.english: To put one's hands together in prayer before the worship hall.

examples.japanese: この{神社|じんじゃ}の{拝殿|はいでん}は{江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}に{建|た}てられた。
examples.english: This shrine's worship hall was built in the Edo period.

examples.japanese: {初詣|はつもうで}で{拝殿|はいでん}に{向|む}かう{長|なが}い{列|れつ}ができていた。
examples.english: A long line of people had formed heading toward the worship hall for the New Year's first shrine visit.

notes:
Compound of {拝|はい} ('to worship; to pray') and {殿|でん} ('hall; palace'). In Shinto shrine architecture, the {拝殿|はいでん} is the public-facing building where worshippers pray. It is distinct from the {本殿|ほんでん} (main sanctuary), which houses the enshrined deity and is usually off-limits to the public.

SHRINE ARCHITECTURE:
- The typical layout places the {拝殿|はいでん} in front, connected or adjacent to the {本殿|ほんでん} behind it
- Not all shrines have a separate {拝殿|はいでん} — smaller shrines may have only a {本殿|ほんでん}
- The {拝殿|はいでん} often features a {賽銭箱|さいせんばこ} (offering box) and {鈴|すず} (bell) at its front

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {拝殿|はいでん}で{参拝|さんぱい}する: to worship at the hall of worship
- {拝殿|はいでん}の{前|まえ}: in front of the worship hall
- {拝殿|はいでん}に{向|む}かって{礼|れい}をする: to bow toward the worship hall
- {拝殿|はいでん}の{建|た}て{替|か}え: rebuilding of the worship hall

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {本殿|ほんでん}: main sanctuary — the innermost, most sacred building that houses the deity; usually not open to the public
- {社殿|しゃでん}: shrine buildings — a collective term for all the buildings in a shrine complex
- {本堂|ほんどう}: main hall (Buddhist) — the equivalent central worship building in a Buddhist temple
